payload.reason: The evidence indicates that setting the vector dimension to 10 empirically leads to a token distribution that approximates the Zipfian distribution, suggesting a relationship between vector dimensionality and the statistical properties of language.

claims.text: Setting the vector dimension to 10 causes the token distribution to approximate the Zipfian distribution due to empirical findings from experiments.
Natural language follows a Zipfian distribution, which is characterized by the relationship between word frequency and rank, and this property is captured when the vector dimension is set to 10.
